title.narrative: ARGENTINA Annual Action Plan 2025 - Sustainable raw materials value chains between the EU and Argentina

description.narrative: SummaryThe context of the Action is the EU-Argentina Critical Raw Materials Memorandum of Understanding and the concretization of its Roadmap of activities. It seeks to leverage and support the priorities of the national Government and the provinces to transform Argentina¿s mining sector into a sustainable and high-performing economic driver, and the EU¿s ambition to promote responsible and resilient CRM supply chains that deliver mutual benefits for both Argentina and the EU. At the same time, it seeks to cater to the priorities of the EU private sector.Recent development of the mining regions hold the potential to further strengthen the EU-Argentina partnership, given Argentina¿s strong potential in the supply of lithium, copper, and potentially rare earth elements. These resources are critical for the EU¿s green and digital transitions, industrial resilience, and geopolitical autonomy. The resources also hold the potential to create new jobs in Argentina, offering economic and social development to a region broadly marginalised from the EU¿s industrial value chains.The Action aims to play a catalyst role for private sector investment into critical raw materials projects (¿EU-Argentina CRM Catalyst¿) focussing on the development of CRM projects in Argentina that are of strategic interest to the EU. The ultimate aim is to contribute to secure sustainable, resilient, and responsible supply chains that are mutually beneficial for Argentina and the EU. Its implementation will be done in coordination with DG GROW¿s call for strategic projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act, and the CRM Facility, which involves close monitoring, analysis, and dialogue with project promoters to identify and prioritise key projects along the CRM value chain.This Action contributes to the 360-degree approach, improving the conditions for investment in Argentina¿s mining sector and creating opportunities for European actors across CRM value chains. It targets four key areas with strong development potential, aiming to enhance investment conditions and facilitate EU engagement throughout different segments of the value chain:1)    Enabling infrastructure - such as electric transmission lines, renewable energy, and sustainable transport modalities ¿ current lack of infrastructure hampers large-scale mining investments. Several projects of strategic interest to the EU are geographically clustered, responding to the need for joint efforts to develop infrastructure. The Action will support the preparation of coordinated, bankable investment plans - potentially through PPPs - by mobilising technical assistance, building strong business cases that can attract financing from Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and International Finance Institutions (IFIs) under Global Gateway.
